questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me that the language spoken at my study destination made sense in connection to my education. Another really crucial aspect was the courses that the university had to offer. I wanted to use my time abroad to not only experience a new culture but also to strengthen my academic profile with courses that were different from what my home university had to offer.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You are in charge of making your time studying abroad a good or bad experience. Of course, there are going to be things that are out of your control but how you choose to spend your free time or how engaged you are in finding new friends is up to you. And that has a massive effect on your overall experience of studying abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A lot of the information you needed upon arrival was emailed to you prior to your arrival, and if you had any questions you had the opportunity to contact the department of the university in charge of exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My host university had students waiting at the airport to greet you if you arrived at certain times. However, I did not use this assistance as I had planned to arrive before and explore some places.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding housing can be a very hard and time-consuming task. I would recommend you start looking for housing early.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living in Canada can be expensive, so adjust your expectations to match the realities of the housing opportunities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived with roommates from my home country that I found using a Facebook group for other exchange students going to Canada. So if you want to live with other people from your home country, then be active and use the tools available for students going abroad.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a website where you can look at the courses, see what times they are offered throughout the week and create a schedule based on the courses you would like as long as they do not overlap each other.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You always had the opportunity to contact people from the host university regarding any questions you might have.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: After getting a "forhåndgodkendelse" for the classes I wanted, I was very successful when registering for the classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you choose a university that offers a number of courses you find interesting as you are not guaranteed to get the courses you apply for.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses had a heaver reading/assignment load than others.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a mix of lectures and seminars depending on the course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Citizenship
Globalization, Social Justice and Human Rights
Peace, Justice, Human Rights
Gender, Race, Culture, Power
Introduction to linguistics: Words, Sentences and Meaning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Out of the five courses I took the one called "Global Citizenship" was my favorite. The course covered and discussed some interesting topics and the professor was very enthusiastic about teaching the course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I do not think I had any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The mobile subscription was more expensive than I thought it would be.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university had a gym where you could train, as well as different groups you could join. The university also held different sports events that could attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to some of the football/other sports matches, the outdoor clubs "Sunday hike" or some of other different social events held by the university and its students. The Sunday hikes are a great place to meet new people. Some people attend in groups, others on their own, but everyone walks together and talks to whoever is near by.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hang out with friends, travel, and relax. Do not feel pressured to do it all, but when you have the space both mentally and time-wise, then use it and explore your local neighborhood or other places around the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Canada is not drastically different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: For me arriving early and engaging in conversations seemed to be the trick to meeting new people. It can seem intimidating to start a conversation with a stranger, but you will be happy once you dare to cross that barrier.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing, that I can think of.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A lot of the Canadian people I meet were very polite and happy to get to know you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. A positive mindset goes a long way.
2. Everything is going to be very new and might be a bit overwhelming at times, so allow yourself to take a step back and spend some you-time every once in a while
3. Explore what the univerisity and city has to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are in doubt about anything, just text the university. They want to help you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The courses I took were cool, but it was the social life that really made my time abroad special.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living with new roommates.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
